contenders.handicapper_notes: Second-up today after showing good tactical toe on debut over 1100m here at Narromine when beaten just 3.2 lengths in a solid country maiden. Most seasoned maiden campaigner in the field with multiple minor placings. Finished third over 1200m at Warren in strong country maiden grade three starts back. Possesses reliable tactical speed (P style) and gets the ideal inside gate to utilize the pronounced Narromine on-pace bias.

Ran a pleasing fifth first-up at Dubbo over 1000m where he made up late ground. Previously placed third over 1300m at Orange when dictating terms from the front. Peak physical condition 2nd-up and maps to settle in the first four from an advantageous low draw.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Boasts premier track-and-distance credentials, having narrowly missed by 0.3L over this exact 1600m circuit two starts ago. Followed with a resilient third at Dubbo behind Proper Twelve and another solid placing at Wellington. Gets ideal tactical setup as a presser (P) who will settle in the first two, perfectly matching the on-pace bias of the short 300m Narromine straight. Faces top-weight tax at 59.0kg, but his hard-knocking regional stamina gives him a distinct edge over this field.

Drawn ideally in barrier 4 to secure the gun run stalking just behind the speed as a presser (P). Has proven effective at the 1600m journey with multiple tight placings in Country Class 1 company. Carries 57.0kg under Ken Dunbar and gets conditions to suit on a firming Good 3 surface where inside saving runs count double.

Strong Dubbo maiden winner three starts back who finished only 2.9L off Proper Twelve when trying 1600m for the first time. Clint Lundholm and Kody Nestor combination commands respect. As a swooper (S) who tends to drop out early, the flat circuit and 300m home stretch present a tactical challenge, but he possesses the field best raw sectional burst if within striking range.

Well suited back up to 1600m after finding 1400m too sharp at Wellington last Tuesday on a quick back-up. Demonstrated stamina two runs back when charging into 2nd over the mile at Moree. Sits midfield (S) and apprentice Izzy Neale will give her every chance from a workable middle draw.

The probable pacesetter and clear speed element (E) of the race. Led for a long way over 1400m at Wellington last start before checking in fourth. Steps up to 1600m for the first time, but if apprentice Jacob Stiff can cross cleanly and dictate soft fractions on this leader-biased track, she will take serious catching.

Raced handy and stayed on stoutly when beaten only one length over the Wellington mile on September 15. Benefits from the featherweight 55.0kg assignment under Mikayla Weir. Barrier 12 is tricky on this tight layout, but she has the tactical versatility (P) to slot in and contend for exotics.
